jobs.description:
Morgan Stanley Community Development Finance is seeking a senior-level Affordable Housing Finance Product Manager to lead the end-to-end management of the Firm’s affordable housing private equity investment portfolio. The role will oversee the full investment lifecycle—from sourcing and origination through underwriting, transaction approval, closing, portfolio and asset management, governance, risk monitoring, performance reporting, and investment exits.

This individual will serve as a senior product owner and relationship manager for affordable housing private equity strategies, working closely with internal stakeholders, fund managers, sponsors, legal counsel, risk partners, and other control functions to ensure disciplined execution, strong portfolio performance, and alignment with Morgan Stanley’s community development, risk management, and business objectives.

Note: Location is open within the the U.S.

Responsibilities

Oversee the affordable housing private equity product strategy and portfolio management framework, including origination priorities, investment guidelines, portfolio objectives, performance targets, and exit planning.
Lead sourcing and originations for new affordable housing private equity investment opportunities, including evaluation of fund managers, sponsors, markets, investment structures, projected returns, community development impact, and strategic fit.
Oversee due diligence, underwriting, financial analysis, market review, sponsor and guarantor assessment, legal documentation, and transaction approval materials for new investments and follow-on commitments.
Present investment opportunities, portfolio updates, risk matters, and strategic recommendations to transaction council, senior management, credit partners, and other internal governance forums.
Serve as the primary relationship manager for affordable housing private equity fund managers, developers, sponsors, and other external partners, ensuring strong communication, accountability, and execution.
Manage post-closing portfolio oversight, periodic asset reviews, compliance monitoring, operating performance analysis, capital account tracking, distribution forecasting, valuation support, and watchlist management.
Monitor fund and underlying asset performance against underwriting expectations, investment agreements, regulatory requirements, and CRA objectives.
Represent Morgan Stanley on fund advisory boards, investor committees, and other governance bodies, providing guidance on consents, amendments, waivers, workouts, dispositions, and other material portfolio matters.
Partner with internal risk stake holders to ensure appropriate controls, approvals, reporting, and issue resolution.
Lead, mentor, and develop staff supporting affordable housing private equity products, promoting strong execution standards, analytical rigor, and consistent portfolio management practices.

Skills Required

Deep understanding of affordable housing finance, private equity fund structures, LIHTC investments, multi-family real estate underwriting, asset management, and portfolio risk management.
Strong financial modeling, valuation, credit analysis, cash flow forecasting, and investment performance assessment skills.
Proven ability to evaluate complex transactions, identify risks, develop mitigation strategies, and make sound investment recommendations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex investment, risk, and portfolio matters clearly to senior management and governance committees.
Strong relationship management and negotiation skills with demonstrated ability to work effectively with fund managers, developers, sponsors, legal counsel, and internal control partners.
Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities, transactions, portfolio matters, and deadlines in a complex institutional environment.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word; experience with portfolio reporting systems, investment databases, and data visualization tools preferred.

Experience

15+ years of relevant experience in affordable housing finance, private equity, multi-family real estate investment, asset management, credit, or portfolio management.
Demonstrated experience managing investments across the full lifecycle, including origination, underwriting, approval, closing, construction or stabilization monitoring, ongoing asset management, workouts or restructurings, and exits.
Experience with public sector financing sources and regulatory frameworks, including Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, HUD/FHA programs, tax-exempt bonds, state and local housing programs, and other community development tools.
Established relationships with affordable housing developers, fund managers, lenders, investors, public agencies, and other industry participants preferred.
Prior experience leading teams, managing senior stakeholder relationships, and operating within a regulated financial institution or similarly complex investment platform strongly preferred.

Job Summary

Under the general direction of the Executive Director of Development, the Director of Development for the College of Business develops and executes strategies to secure philanthropic support for San José State University fundraising priorities identified by the University’s leadership in collaboration with the Office of Development in the Division of University Advancement. Responsibilities include but are not limited to identifying, qualifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding individuals capable of giving major gifts to the University. In support of these efforts, the Director of Development initiates, maintains and strengthens close working relationships with key academic leaders, campus administrators, various stakeholders, and University Advancement colleague.

Manage an assigned prospect portfolio of key individuals supporting university fundraising priorities
Coordinate with Prospect Research Team to expand and enhance a prospect pipeline that aligns with university and campaign priorities
Actively manage a prospect / donor portfolio with annual goals for personal visits and fundraising outcomes based on established metrics
Develop and execute sound strategies to identify, cultivate, solicit and steward major gift prospects/donors – initiate contact, develop appropriate cultivation plans, and move individuals in an appropriate and timely fashion toward solicitation and closure
Present and regularly review top prospect strategies and immediate supervisor and other key team members as appropriate
Work collaboratively with the leadership of colleges, key university administrators and other stakeholders, offering them counsel on donor-centric cultivation and solicitation strategy, as appropriate
Work collaboratively with peers in Major Gifts as well as colleagues in Annual Giving, Planned giving and Corporate and Foundation Relations

Collaborate with stewardship colleagues with donor stewardship efforts particularly pertaining to the Division of Research and Innovation and help promote a culture of gratitude among internal and external constituents
Effectively utilize campus data management system and enter prospect/donor contact reports and their relevant data in a timely fashion
Prepare written donor cultivation and solicitation plans and proposals
Participate in staff, functional and strategy meetings including prospect review sessions, attend conferences, seminars, and other development training as feasible and appropriate

Job Overview

The Associate Director of Development plays a critical role in advancing the University’s fundraising priorities by strategically managing a comprehensive donor pipeline. This position is responsible for the full lifecycle of donor engagement including identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship activities. It requires exceptional time management and organizational skills to effectively prioritize and move prospects through each stage while maintaining momentum across a diverse portfolio. Success in this role depends on strong communication abilities to clearly articulate the University’s mission and impact while building trust and meaningful relationships with a broad range of constituents.

A key focus of the position is frontline fundraising with a special focus on gifts requiring demonstrated success across both annual giving and major giving, in the $5k-$25k+ range. The Associate Director applies strategic thinking to assess donor readiness, align opportunities with institutional priorities, and move prospects thoughtfully from initial engagement to major gift consideration. This work is grounded in a disciplined approach to planning and execution, supported by a strong work ethic and a commitment to achieving measurable results that contribute to divisional and university wide fundraising goals.

The role also emphasizes the use of data informed strategies to guide decision making and portfolio management. By analyzing donor trends, engagement metrics, and giving patterns, the Associate Director develops targeted approaches that enhance effectiveness and maximize philanthropic outcomes. This analytical mindset, combined with sound judgment and adaptability, ensures that efforts remain focused, efficient, and aligned with evolving institutional needs.

Collaboration is central to the success of this position, as the Associate Director works closely with internal partners and external stakeholders to maximize philanthropic opportunities. The ability to effectively engage, influence, and coordinate with colleagues, donors, and community members is essential to building a strong culture of philanthropy. Through these efforts, the Associate Director advances the University’s mission and upholds its commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and access, fostering an environment where philanthropy supports broad and meaningful institutional impact.

*** To be considered for this position candidate must be serving permanently in the title of City Planner, or be reachable on the open competitive civil service list for Exam No. 5045. ***

Transit Development (TD), within NYC DOT’s Division of Transportation Planning & Management (TPM), is responsible for developing public transit-supportive street infrastructure and policies to improve mobility for all New Yorkers The unit manages the bus-related components of the NYC Streets Plan, including the Bus Action Plan and transit policy initiatives and develops location-specific projects to help the quality and safety of bus operations, and to improve pedestrian access to transit. TD also serves as a resource to the agency on public transit related matters, including acting as one of the key points of contact with the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA).

TD seeks to hire a candidate to help oversee a sub-unit tasked with developing new and improved rapid bus service in conjunction with MTA to further the goals of the Mayor and the NYC Streets Plan. The candidate would work to develop infrastructure-intensive bus projects that reshape the built environment to bring quality transit service to all New Yorkers. The candidate would assist with oversight of a team that, among other duties: 1) conducts extensive community-centered public outreach; 2) pursues and manages grants to finance projects; 3) navigates environmental review; 4) tracks project development; 5) develop designs in coordination with other sub-units; 6) coordinates with the MTA on bus operations; and 7) initiates capital projects. The selected candidate would also be expected to help hire and develop staff, and to develop and present executive briefing materials. The candidate would meet extensively with the general public, work with community boards and other public stakeholders in public workshops, presentations, and other settings, including evening and weekend work. This is an opportunity to work in a high-profile, fast-paced public sector environment with a team dedicated to improving safety, accessibility, and mobility throughout New York City.

The Division of Transportation Planning & Management is responsible for the safe, efficient, and environmentally responsible movement of people and goods on the City's streets, supporting the larger goals of economic and social vitality for people living, working, and doing business in New York City. The Division’s responsibilities include planning, street design, technical analysis, signs, transit development, freight mobility, and markings, ensuring the safety of motor vehicle occupants, pedestrians, and cyclists.

jobs.description:
Chief Operating Officer

Multi-Location Dermatology & Aesthetics Practice

Atlanta, GA — four locations

Our Mission
We provide our families with compassionate skin care and medical education, giving them the comfort and confidence to live healthy and beautiful lives. We put our patients first, work to constantly improve our patients' experience, and demand excellence from our entire team.

Our Vision
Everyone deserves healthy skin.

Our Values
• Patient-focused
• Team-focused
• Community-focused

The Opportunity
The Chief Operating Officer is the senior-most administrative executive in the organization, reporting directly to the two physician Owners. The COO is accountable for the operational and financial performance of all four clinics and the aesthetics division, leads the practice's management team, and partners with the Owners on strategic planning, growth, and major business decisions. The COO carries direct accountability for revenue growth and EBITDA performance across the practice.
The COO is expected to lead through the management team and hold vendors accountable rather than absorb work personally, and to build an operating structure that does not depend on any single person. The practice operates without a CEO layer, which means real authority, exposure, and a short line to decisions.
The right candidate is someone energized by building operating discipline, developing managers into stronger leaders, and bringing clarity to a growing organization that has significant room to execute.

Key Responsibilities
Executive and Strategic Leadership
• Partner with the physician Owners on strategic planning, growth initiatives, service line expansion, and major capital and business decisions
• Translate ownership objectives into annual operating plans with named owners, deadlines, and measurable outcomes
• Serve as the point of resolution for cross-departmental priorities, escalations, and resource decisions
• Return the Owners' time to clinical care and strategic direction by taking genuine ownership of operations

Financial Leadership
• Own the operating budget, forecast, and expense discipline across all locations and the aesthetics division
• Drive EBITDA growth and margin improvement, with accountability for both revenue performance and the cost structure that supports it
• Establish a disciplined monthly close and financial review rhythm, working with the practice's accounting resources and external CPA firm
• Help define and build out the internal finance function, then lead through it
• Deliver location-level profit and loss visibility, including appropriate separation of administrative overhead from operating locations
• Monitor and improve revenue cycle performance in collaboration with the Billing Manager
• Own payer relationships and lead the renegotiation of managed care contracts, including reimbursement terms for advanced practice providers
• Understand expense and payroll growth at the line-item level and hold cost growth in a defensible relationship to revenue growth
• Oversee payroll, compensation structure, and performance-based incentive programs

Operations and Team Leadership
• Lead a management team spanning HR, finance, billing, call center, Mohs, dermatopathology, aesthetics, and site management across four locations
• Oversee the recently launched dermatopathology service line and lead the development of an in-house laboratory
• Chair the weekly management team meeting and maintain a consistent one-on-one cadence with all direct reports
• Maintain regular on-site presence across locations to ensure consistent standards, staffing, and patient experience
• Coordinate provider schedules across sites to maximize patient access
• Build and maintain an operating dashboard covering access, provider productivity, revenue cycle, patient experience, staffing and turnover, aesthetics performance, and progress against strategic initiatives

Aesthetics Division
• Own the operational and financial performance of the aesthetics division, including service and product mix, pricing, provider productivity, inventory, and reconciliation
• Bring or develop genuine commercial depth in aesthetics as a growth line rather than as an adjunct to medical dermatology

People and Culture
• Direct hiring, performance review cycles, and personnel decisions in partnership with HR
• Manage the PEO relationship, including annual benefits selection and renewal
• Develop managers into stronger leaders through coaching, clear expectations, and accountability
• Build staffing pipelines for clinical and administrative roles, with candidate pools for high-turnover positions and succession plans for key roles, so vacancies are filled from a bench rather than from a standing start
• Own retention as a measured outcome, particularly in clinical support roles

Vendors, Technology and Facilities
• Own vendor selection, contract review and negotiation, and renewal management across IT, marketing, telecommunications, software, and clinical supply
• Oversee the managed IT services relationship and the practice management and EMR platform. This role directs and holds vendors accountable; it does not perform hands-on technical work
• Manage facilities and lease matters, including negotiations, amendments, and tenant improvement projects, with an eye toward potential practice acquisition of current or future office space
• Oversee inventory and procurement systems across all sites

Compliance and Clinical Operations Support
• Coordinate with the Compliance Officer to maintain regulatory readiness across all locations
• Build the operational infrastructure for new clinical service lines as the practice expands
• Support clinical leadership on provider workflow, capacity, and coverage planning

How This Role Works
The practice uses the Working Genius framework to understand how people contribute and where they thrive. We are being direct about the working style this role requires, because fit matters here as much as the resume.

Candidates advancing in the process will be invited to complete a Working Genius assessment. There is no single correct result. It is used to have an honest conversation about fit and about how the role and the surrounding team work best together.

This role will suit someone who is energized by:
• Exercising judgment.
• Supporting and developing other people.
• Rallying people to action.
• Finishing things.
• Delegating deliberately.

What Success Looks Like in the First 12 Months
• A documented responsibility map is in place, with work positioned where it belongs rather than concentrated by default
• The management team operates with clear expectations, a consistent cadence, and defined decision rights
• Monthly financial close and review run on a predictable rhythm, with location-level reporting the Owners trust
• Expense and payroll growth are understood at the line-item level and managed against plan
• EBITDA is measured and reported with a clear improvement plan agreed with the Owners
• Managed care contracts have been reviewed and a renegotiation plan is underway
• Provider schedules stay full and patient access improves across all four locations
• The aesthetics division has clear performance measures and reconciliation that closes on time
• Vendor contracts and renewals are actively managed with no unplanned auto-renewals or lapses
• Retention in clinical support roles is measured, understood, and improving
• The Owners spend their time on clinical care and strategic direction, not daily operations

Qualifications
• Minimum 5 years of progressive operations leadership in multi-site healthcare, with direct profit and loss accountability
• Demonstrated success leading managers across multiple locations and functions
• Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis and financial reporting, with the ability to interrogate the numbers and hold the finance function to account
• Demonstrated track record of improving EBITDA or operating margin across a multi-site organization
• Experience negotiating and executing vendor contracts, leases, and service agreements
• Working fluency across HR, IT, compliance, and facilities functions, sufficient to direct specialists and vendors
• EMR or practice management platform experience; ModMed (EMA) preferred
• A self-starter who can identify issues, exercise sound judgment, and take initiative
• Master’s degree preferred; qualified candidates without one are encouraged to apply
• Dermatology, aesthetics, or specialty physician practice experience strongly preferred
• Experience in physician-owned private practice, particularly reporting directly to owners without a CEO layer, preferred
• Experience building or maturing a finance and reporting function, rather than only inheriting one, preferred
• Commercial experience in aesthetics, medical spa, or retail-adjacent healthcare services preferred
• Experience negotiating or renegotiating managed care and payer contracts preferred
• Experience with commercial lease negotiation or property acquisition preferred
• Experience launching or scaling ancillary service lines, such as pathology or laboratory services, preferred

Compensation and Work Environment
• Base salary starting at $200,000, commensurate with experience, with a performance-based incentive component
• Full-time and on-site
• Benefits provided through the practice's PEO
• Physician-owned and independent, with no private equity involvement

Apply for This Position

All inquiries will be held in strict confidence, the identity of the practice will be shared with candidates at the appropriate stage of the process.

Strategic Leadership and Vision

Regularly review the strategic plan and report progress to ensure that priorities and resources align.
Anticipate industry disruption and guide the organization through change using data, technology, and innovation as differentiators, without creating unnecessary disruption.
Serve as a strategic advisor to the Board, providing thought leadership, industry insights, and recommendations that support informed decision-making and organizational success.

Oversee the planning, implementation, and evaluation of the organization's programs and services, working with board committee chairpersons.

This role involves conducting thorough data analysis and leveraging insights from employee feedback to craft engagement initiatives that foster a positive and collaborative work environment and cultivate an exceptional organizational culture. The Director will lead efforts to ensure an inclusive and positive work environment. Additionally, the Director oversees training and development programs to enhance employee growth, development, and retention. The Director's leadership ensures that UDRI remains a thriving and cohesive workplace community.

10 years of progressive HR experience, including leadership across multiple HR disciplines
Five years of experience leading and managing teams
Expertise across HR functional areas, including knowledge of federal/state HR regulations and experience mitigating risk

Experience with succession planning, performance systems, and leadership development
Experience leading the strategy, design, administration, and compliance of employer-sponsored benefit programs, including health, welfare, and retirement plans

HR certification such as SHRM-SCP or SPHR

Valid driver’s license, with a low risk driving record, and insurable by the University
